redWitnesses.claim: no corner-SHAPE token axis — the corner RADIUS is tokenized (--radius-{xs..3xl,pill} + semantic aliases) but the corner SHAPE is a hardcoded `squircle` keyword in two CSS files, no --corner-k-* / --corner-shape-* companion
redWitnesses.codeEvidence: grep 'corner-k-\|corner-shape-' src/styles/theme.css = NONE at HEAD; theme.css:28-65 is the radius half only
redWitnesses.disposition: GREEN — theme.css mints --corner-k-{squircle:2,soft:1.7,sharp:2.4} (squircle == superellipse(2) == n=4 per MDN) + the semantic --corner-shape-{card:round,pill:round,panel:round,bigdock:superellipse(var(--corner-k-squircle))} POLICY aliases in the leading plain @theme.

redWitnesses.claim: the policy is INVERTED — corner-shape: squircle is applied to .glass-card/.glass-btn/.btn-pill (cards + icon-buttons + pills), directly contradicting the user's 'rounded for cards'
redWitnesses.disposition: GREEN — the glass.css squircle block is RE-HOMED OFF cards/buttons/pills (DELETED; they resolve --corner-shape-card/-pill == round — no corner-shape decl). A policy comment records the no-re-add rule. Clean break, no alias.

redWitnesses.claim: the big-dock corner shape is a bare hardcoded `squircle` keyword, not a token — not :root-overridable, W42's dock-morph cannot calc() a k against it
redWitnesses.codeEvidence: dock.css:539 corner-shape: squircle (bare keyword inside the @supports block)
redWitnesses.disposition: GREEN — dock.css reads corner-shape: var(--corner-shape-bigdock) — as token-overridable as the radius; W42 reads the SAME --corner-k-squircle vocabulary.

redWitnesses.claim: the @supports condition tests the keyword `squircle`, not the literal-2 feature query — the token resolves to superellipse(var(--corner-k-squircle)) and var() is not @supports-evaluable
redWitnesses.disposition: GREEN — the big-dock gate is @supports (corner-shape: superellipse(2)) (the literal feature query, the same Chrome-139 feature); the un-gated border-radius round stays the cross-engine contract.

redWitnesses.claim: the clip-path-fallback REJECTION is unrecorded — a later agent might 'fix' the 35% Safari gap with a JS path generator (which hard-clips the box, severing the backdrop-filter blur halo + the cartoon offset-shadow)
redWitnesses.codeEvidence: no DECISION in src/ or the wave docs rejecting the clip-path figma-squircle cross-engine fallback
redWitnesses.disposition: GREEN — the rejection is recorded in the wave doc (§Scope fold 4 + §SOTA + §PreceptAlignment) + the glass.css/dock.css policy comments; the gate locks the @supports-over-border-radius-round shape (no clip-path).

liveArmNotes.magnitudes: --corner-k-squircle: 2 (squircle, n=4 — the canonical web squircle); --corner-k-soft: 1.7 (n≈3.4); --corner-k-sharp: 2.4 (n≈4.8); --corner-shape-card/pill/panel: round; --corner-shape-bigdock: superellipse(var(--corner-k-squircle)).
liveArmNotes.liveChecks: On a real Chrome-139 @ localhost:5173 over the dock route (/navigation/dock): (1) getComputedStyle('.glass-dock.shape-card').cornerShape === 'superellipse(2)' (the big-dock squircle paints — backdrop-filter + cartoon shadow follow the silhouette, not a plain rounded arc); (2) getComputedStyle('.glass-card').cornerShape === 'round'/'normal' (the re-home canary — cards stay round); (3) on Safari/Firefox (or CSS.supports('corner-shape','superellipse(2)') === false) the big-dock falls back to the border-radius round arc with no broken paint; (4) no dock-morph / glass-material regression, light AND dark. TUNE: if the big-dock squircle reads too square at k=2, the orchestrator dials --corner-k-squircle (or --corner-shape-bigdock to --corner-k-soft=1.7) live; if a large-radius surface ('and the like') is opted in, re-point its --corner-shape-<surface> at superellipse(var(--corner-k-squircle)).
